qualification.provider_error: Invalid tool parameters schema: object is not accepted inside the public adapter's nullable type-array encoding.

control.conclusion: Network, credential, endpoint, model, thinking mode, and streaming are healthy.

schema_audit.official_rule: DeepSeek strict mode supports object and anyOf; every object is closed with all properties required, and the live validator requires each schema node to carry type, anyOf, or $ref.

operations: Rewrite only the two object|null type arrays as anyOf(object,null), moving object-only properties, required, and additionalProperties into the object branch.
Add type:string to each enum-only node only when every enum value is a string.
Leave the four primitive|null type arrays and every other schema value unchanged.

privacy: All eight diagnostic calls were source-free. Only HTTP status/error identifiers, fixed field names, schema pointers/counts, request field names, byte counts/hashes, and aggregate response bytes were retained. No API key, repository source, prompt packet, response text/reasoning, tool arguments/results, durable identity, header, or host path was persisted.
not_environment_or_network: The no-tools command-line control returned HTTP 200 with streaming reasoning, the raw strict-tools request returned a structured HTTP 400 schema error, and the minimally projected strict-tools request returned HTTP 200 on the same endpoint/model/key/network.
next_step: Keep T084/T085 blocked. Correct AD-19 so the public adapter schemas are immutable inputs to one deterministic DeepSeek strict projection rather than the accepted wire itself; add test-first drift and fail-closed coverage, then rerun T096/T083.
summary: T096 exposed a second request-contract defect: byte-identical raw public adapter declarations are not DeepSeek-strict compatible. A bounded two-rule deterministic schema projection makes the same source-free V4 request succeed.
